overview.title: Index: L to M (seq2seq to models)

overview.importance: It points to the LLM material (pretrained LLMs, RLHF, RAG, reasoning models, LoRA, mini-GPT) and to the machine-learning fundamentals.

concepts.name: LLMs (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 468, 495–504, 565 (PDF 492, 519–528, 589). Sub-entries: using pretrained 484–494, RLHF 495–498, multimodal 498–501, RAG 501, reasoning models 502–504.
concepts.intuition: PDF 492 introduces LLMs, PDF 508–528 uses and extends them, and PDF 589 is the critique in chapter 19.
concepts.technical: Related entries: mini-GPT 470–484, LoRA 490–494, instruction fine-tuning 488–490.
concepts.significance: LLMs are the book's state-of-the-art generative models.
concepts.misconception: Printed 565 is about the limits of LLMs, not how to use them.

concepts.name: LoRA (index entry)
concepts.definition: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is indexed at printed 490–494 (PDF 514–518). enable_lora() is at 492.
concepts.intuition: LoRA fine-tunes a large pretrained model cheaply by training small low-rank update matrices.
concepts.technical: Beyond the index: LoRA freezes W and learns ΔW = BA with a small rank r. This explanation is not on this page.
concepts.significance: It makes fine-tuning practical on modest hardware.
concepts.misconception: LoRA does not retrain all of the model's weights.

concepts.name: machine learning (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 2, 3, 136, 171 (PDF 26, 27, 160, 195). Sub-entries: evaluating models 149–153, the universal workflow 179–189.
concepts.intuition: Chapters 5 and 6 (PDF 160–213) are the methodology core of the book.
concepts.significance: These pages turn model building into a repeatable process.
concepts.example: Open PDF 203 for the universal workflow.
concepts.misconception: Machine learning is not the same thing as deep learning. Deep learning is a subfield of it.
